Jimmy Tata backs Tata Sons listing, accuses Noel of ‘back-door takeover’
 He urged the RBI to enforce strict listing timelines and prevent any breakup of the group, while calling on the government and Charity Commissioner to safeguard the trusts’ founding objectives.
 Updated - November 17, 2026 08:49 am IST 
 Lalatendu Mishra READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Amid an intensifying power struggle within the Tata Group, Jimmy Naval Tata, 85, younger brother of late Ratan Tata, has thrown his weight behind the listing of Tata Sons, accusing Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata of attempting a “back-door takeover” of the holding company by inducting family members into key trusts.
 In a strongly worded communication responding to queries from a Tata stalwart, believed to be Tata Trusts trustee Vijay Singh, Mr. Jimmy Tata alleged that the composition of the trusts was being altered to consolidate family control over Tata Sons.
 Why to tinker with something that has delivered value for 150 years: Noel Tata “In recent time the trusts are being filled with family members of the present Tata Trust Chairman, [Noel Tata] thereby securing a degree of control over Tata Sons that was never the settlors’ intention,” he said.
 “It is entirely inappropriate for more than one family member to serve on a given trust; doing so effectively confers ownership rights over the trusts’ significant shareholding in Tata Sons at no consideration whatsoever. Such an arrangement is untenable and amounts to a back-door takeover of Tata Sons,” he added.
 Mr. Jimmy Tata, a trustee of several Tata Trusts, said the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) and Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) were established by their respective founders, who had no children, to serve the larger public interest.
 “The trusts were established for the benefit of the Indian people—as laid out in the objects of the trusts (alleviation of poverty and safeguarding Indian culture)—and the trustees were custodians of public trusts that can never be dissolved, unlike private family trusts,” he said, adding that Mr. JRD Tata and his father, Mr. Naval Tata, were conscious of this responsibility.
 Tata feud: Venu Srinivasan, Vijay Singh hit back at Khambata, accuse him of ignoring governance failures Backing Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, Mr. Jimmy Tata credited him with turning around heavily indebted group companies, delivering record earnings and dividend payouts exceeding 6,500%, including to Tata Sons shareholders.
 Despite overwhelming support for Mr. Chandrasekaran, including a 4-1 vote on the Tata Sons board and a unanimous Tata Trusts resolution, Mr. Noel allegedly sought to block him by invoking veto provisions in the amended Articles of Association without offering justification.
 “These developments make the listing of Tata Sons, as mandated by the RBI, all the more critical,” he said.
 According to Mr. Jimmy Tata, listing would end the group’s “pervasive culture of secrecy”, strengthen statutory accountability and necessitate changes to the Articles of Association. He also cited the successful public listing of TCS under Ratan Tata as evidence of its benefits.
 Tata Sons rejects Noel's request for audio-video recording of September 17 boardmeet Rejecting Mr. Noel’s proposed restructuring, he warned that breaking up Tata Sons into smaller entities to circumvent RBI listing requirements would be “deeply damaging and contrary to public and shareholder interests”.
 He urged the RBI to enforce strict listing timelines and prevent any breakup of the group, while calling on the government and Charity Commissioner to safeguard the trusts’ founding objectives.
 Mr. Jimmy Tata also blamed amendments to the Articles of Association around 2013-14 for concentrating power in the hands of the Tata Trusts chairman. The changes, he alleged, introduced “unnatural, dictatorial veto powers” and the right to nominate directors, undermining collective board authority.
 Tata Trusts within right to seek merger, but Tata Sons can challenge: Lawyer He further questioned the four-year tenure limit imposed on certain trustees while others remained exempt, alleging that dissenting trustees were being marginalised. He cited Mr. Venu Srinivasan, whose term expires in December, and Mr. Vijay Singh as examples.
 Contrasting the present leadership with the group’s earlier tradition of appointing independent trustees and nurturing professional talent, Mr. Jimmy Tata named Nani Palkhivala, Gautam Sarabhai, Homi Sethna and Homi Bhabha among past trustees, and Sumant Moolgaokar, Darbari Seth, Xerxes Desai and Rusi Mody among its celebrated executives.
